_comment: Task 52b golden replay baselines. Both missions are the exact same seed-1, 8-operator (4v4) fixture built through Sandata.Headless.HeadlessRunner.BuildOpenGrid(8) and Sandata.Headless.HeadlessRunner.BuildInitialState(8, 1, packingSide) -- the same dense, alternating-faction packing HeadlessRunnerTests and the seed-1 benchmark workload use -- ticked for 40 ticks with MissionTickPolicy.StateHashCadenceTicks=1 and TickLimit=1000. EmptyOrderStream submits no orders (the pure autonomous case). NonEmptyOrderStream submits, at tick 0 through SandataSimulation.SubmitOrder: a MoveAlongPath order for faction 0's entity 1 along the two-node path (4,4)->(12,4), and a Hold order for faction 1's entity 2. Both orders were accepted (no rejection). Every hash below was measured by running a temporary capture test (removed once these values were recorded), never calculated or typed by hand. TickStateHashesHex[i] is SandataSimulation.LastStateHash immediately after RunTick(i), formatted X16.
_rerecorded2026-08-11: Every value except the two tick-0 state hashes was re-measured on 2026-08-11, when SandataSimulation.RunTick began writing MissionState.Tick. Until then nothing in Sandata.Core ever wrote that field, so it stayed 0 for a whole run: SandataStateHasher folded a constant and every emitted event carried tick 0 regardless of when it fired. Both tick-0 state hashes are byte-identical to the values recorded before the fix (D81CEB0CBE66B3D8 and 92AA050E83A47D1B), which is the expected signature of this particular change -- on tick 0 the field was already 0, so only tick 1 onward could move. Both FinalEventHashHex values moved together, from 74E008E940AB05A5, because the events in the feed now carry the tick they fired on. This is NOT a new SandataPresetId: design section 4's trigger list is an enum value or order, a roster order, a weapon weight, the tick rate, the millisecond conversion rule, or a hash mixer, and a defect in RunTick is none of them. SandataRuleset.ContentHash is unchanged at 8955292433887190872.
